note.note:
Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:  Episodic frontal headaches (mostly at work during meetings/computer use) with occasional mild nausea; palpitations ~daily (sometimes triggered in elevator); shortness of breath while sitting at desk (not with exercise); bilateral hand tingling; reduced appetite; ~5 lb unintentional weight loss; decreased libido. Symptoms began after changing jobs; high occupational stress rated 7–8/10. Initial triage noted “feeling hot,” patient emphasized shortness of breath rather than heat intolerance.
- Relevant family medical history:  Not recorded.
- Medications (including OTC or shared medications):  Thyroxine (levothyroxine)—dose/route/frequency not documented. Allergies: No known drug allergies reported.
- Immunisation status reviewed:  Not recorded.
- Sexual and reproductive health:  Decreased libido since job change; otherwise not recorded.
- Physical activity and nutrition:  Physical activity not recorded. Reduced appetite; unintentional ~5 lb weight loss; diet details not recorded.
- Alcohol, tobacco, and substance use:  Alcohol: a couple of glasses of wine about once weekly. Tobacco: non-smoker. Recreational drugs: denied.
- Hearing loss or concerns:  Not recorded.
- Mood/mental health (including depression, self-harm risk):  High work-related stress (7–8/10). Anxiety-like somatic symptoms around work/elevator. Depression symptoms and self-harm risk not recorded.
- Vision problems or recent changes:  Not recorded.
- Family and social relationships, caring responsibilities:  Not recorded.

Examination

- BP, pulse rate and rhythm:  Not recorded (telehealth; in-person exam planned).
- Height, weight, BMI, waist circumference (if indicated):  Not recorded.
- Oral exam (including dentition and gums):  Not recorded.
- Ear exam (otoscopy, whisper test if needed):  Not recorded.
- Vision/eye exam (basic screen):  Not recorded.
- Urinalysis (dipstick for proteinuria):  Not recorded.

Investigations (as indicated)

- Fasting BGL and lipids (or random BGL if needed):  Not recorded.
- Cervical screening (if eligible and due):  Not recorded.
- STI screen (urine or swab – chlamydia/gonorrhoea if age 15–35):  Not recorded.
- Mammogram (if eligible):  Not recorded.
- Other pathology (e.g., HbA1c, iron studies, Vitamin D):  Thyroid function tests planned.

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Key findings: New-onset, work-predominant frontal headaches; palpitations; shortness of breath at rest (desk) but not with exertion; bilateral hand tingling; reduced appetite; mild unintentional weight loss; decreased libido. On thyroxine. High occupational stress since job change.
- Differential diagnoses (aligned with DDx):
  - Work-related anxiety/panic with hyperventilation: High likelihood given temporal relationship to job change, situational triggers (elevator/meetings), SOB at rest but not with exercise, and bilateral hand tingling.
  - Thyroid dysfunction (possible iatrogenic hyperthyroidism from over-replacement): Medium likelihood given thyroxine use with palpitations, weight loss, anxiety-like symptoms, and decreased libido. Requires labs.
  - Tension-type headache (stress/ergonomic-related): Medium likelihood due to frontal headaches during screen time/meetings and high stress.
- Conflicts noted: Patient states “hyperthyroidism” but is taking thyroxine (typically replacement for hypothyroidism). Clarification with labs and prior records needed.
- Working diagnosis and priorities: Probable work-related stress/anxiety with hyperventilation contributing to palpitations, SOB, tingling, and headaches. Rule out thyroid excess/dysfunction. No focal neurologic symptoms reported; weight loss is mild.

Management Plan

- In-person appointment to examine cardiovascular and respiratory systems.
- Blood tests for thyroid function as discussed.
- No medications initiated prior to in-person assessment.
- Patient to book clinic appointment via app; clinician to hand over details to colleagues.

- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits):  Not recorded.
- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral:  Not recorded.
- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support):  Not recorded.
- CTG registration:  Not recorded.
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test):  Not recorded.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):

- Work-related anxiety/panic with hyperventilation – Likelihood: High. Justification: Symptoms began after job change; occur mainly at work; elevator/meeting triggers; SOB at rest but not with exercise; bilateral hand tingling consistent with hyperventilation; reduced appetite/weight loss and decreased libido can accompany stress.
- Thyroid dysfunction (iatrogenic hyperthyroidism from levothyroxine over-replacement) – Likelihood: Moderate. Justification: On thyroxine with palpitations, mild weight loss, anxiety-like symptoms, decreased libido; needs thyroid labs to confirm.
- Tension-type headache (stress/ergonomic) – Likelihood: Moderate. Justification: Frontal headaches during computer/meeting tasks with high stress; limited migrainous features.

Quality checks

- Missing expected elements: BP, pulse, rhythm; height/weight/BMI/waist circumference; full systems exam (oral, ear, vision); urinalysis; immunization review; comprehensive family history; detailed dietary/physical activity history; standardized mental health screening (e.g., GAD-7/PHQ-9); comprehensive alcohol screening; sleep and caffeine intake; occupational/ergonomic assessment; sexual health/STI risk assessment.
- Internal contradictions: Patient reports “hyperthyroidism” but is taking thyroxine (replacement) – conflict noted. Initial triage “feeling hot” vs patient emphasizing shortness of breath; relationship unclear.
- Transcript quality: Telehealth with pauses/partial responses; some unclear segments; no vitals or exam possible.
